# Windows ownership-file access repair

The V3 batch finishes six functional checks valid/restored/released, then stops on
reimagined-baseline-gl46-r1 before scoring. Its owner.json read raises plain
PermissionError(errno13), with no WinError prefix. The earlier retry accepted only
winerror5/32/33 and therefore missed CPython's CRT-backed open failure.

A native exclusive-handle probe reproduces errno13 with winerror=None. The minimal
repair admits Windows EACCES/EPERM without winerror to the existing three-second
bounded read/publication retry. POSIX errors, invalid JSON and permanent denial
still fail; no command is replayed and no ownership/identity check is weakened.
The native regression fixture holds a real exclusive Windows handle, observes
CRT read denial, releases it after150ms, and verifies the maintained reader
recovers. Persistent-denial fixtures retain the time bound.103 benchmark tests
pass on both hosts (3 Asahi/11 Windows platform skips).

The failed baseline is explicitly recovered with --preserve-conflicts after exact
process release. Uncertain FML/Iris/options/selected-pack bytes are retained in its
report before restoring the recorded originals and checking the full world/profile
map. No scored windows exist and the attempt cannot be used as a performance bar.

Before replacing source, all5034 build bindings plus scripts/tests/definitions
were verified and archived. freeze-owned-inputs.py now makes this repeated
preservation procedure reusable; it requires stopped/released/restored reports,
checks exact controller absence, uses capacity admission, verifies every archived
hash and rechecks source hashes and runtime release. Its compact receipt is
native-before-shared-reader-92b154c-20261106.json. The ZIP is also hash-verified
in Asahi's ignored frozen/ directory. Native original report evidence stays intact.

The following scoring queue uses fresh reimagined-baseline-gl46-r1-retry1,
the remaining three modern-context baselines, and the first55 maintained
optimization/control comparisons. Its metadata identifies this controller repair;
rendering implementations are unchanged from the last verified native snapshot.

# First scoring pass repairs

The first batch stopped safely after35/59 operations:30 valid and five invalid.
All35 restored/released with zero remaining clients. Invalid attempts are not
performance results. Replaced native inputs were archived and verified off-host.

- MakeUp G04: the finite Windows constructor capability already exists, but the
  fragment gate and63 shared adapter clauses still restricted that capability to
  Linux. Canonical resources now accept Windows only behind the same finite
  capability; the maintained helper hash is updated. Mac/Linux behavior and full
  native settings remain guarded. Java preprocessing tests verify Windows/Linux
  require the capability and existing assembled combinations remain unchanged.
- MakeUp G05: the draw permission path explicitly requires OpenGL4.1. The failed
  process used actual3.2; retry in real4.6 rather than removing the guard. Its
  original-only4.6 baseline/control cohort must be acquired separately.
- BSL G06: setup explicitly requires OpenGL3.3. The failed process used3.2;
  retry in real4.6 with the existing separate BSL4.6 baseline/control cohort.
- MakeUp G08: the last queued receipt is active with zero of16 captures and no
  error, not a measured nonzero-opacity/RGB difference. The native100 producer
  gate is Linux-only, including the diagnostic writer. Canonical private source
  now admits Windows; a full original-derived Windows preprocessing regression
  verifies schema1023, the diagnostic MRT output and native reference path.
  Numerical equivalence still requires all16 phases and zero errors on hardware.
  Incomplete-capture errors now include concise current-writer state.

The shared G04/G06 entry correction also changes the intended MakeUp G06 entry
route. Preserve its old first-pass timing as the old implementation; reacquire
corrected timings and do not pool implementations into between-process variance.

Local validation:103 benchmark Python tests, three native-cloud builder tests,
and the six selected exact/composition Java tests pass. Native103 Python tests
and exact-graph Java tests pass after safe deployment. BSL G06 in actual4.6 and
MakeUp G08 both finish VALID/restored/released. The cloud check now completes its
required diagnostic coverage rather than timing an inactive writer.

Three MakeUp checks stopped before launch because the shipped recipe referenced
the new fragment helper but Python still read the older authored copy. Corrected
the authored recipe/helper, then used maintained `sync_resources` to verify the
packaged mirrors and update the assembled catalog identity while retaining the
old identity for restoration. A regression test assembles both recipes against
the actual native archive and requires an idempotent resource/catalog sync.
All17 adapter Python tests pass locally; the new actual-archive regression passes
on Windows, followed by a successful offline build and current receipt validation.
No shader/input files were replaced during an operation.

A fifth first-pass failure, BSL G09, requires an OpenGL4.3 compute sampler probe;
the failed process used actual3.2. Its actual image storage already passes the
storage checks. Retry the functional proof and both timing orders in actual4.6,
retaining all sampler/numerical/state-restoration requirements. This does not yet
establish native sampler equivalence or a performance benefit.

MakeUp G04's corrected first hardware check now also passes with restoration.
The fresh97-operation continuation is running, including six remaining functional
checks and91 timing/baseline/control operations. Previous attempts and both
opposite-order timing definitions remain preserved. The analyzer reads newer definitions first and uses actual build-bound
source identities to separate old MakeUp G04/G06 implementations. Old MakeUp G06
timings cannot contribute to the repaired implementation's between-process variance.
All results remain descriptive until repeats, actual work, null controls and
bounded quality have been checked.


The first GL-context continuation launch rejected a malformed new PBR check's
argument order before creating any operation/ledger. Corrected `-u` and the
maintained `check` subcommand positions, validated all97 commands and launched a
fresh owned request. The real queue ledger and START console confirm execution.
The malformed definition is retained as native `scoring-v3-contexts.before-argv-fix.json`;
it has no timing result. The current canonical definition contains only valid CLI
forms. The supported-pack catalog Java regression passes after synchronization.
